title: Halting language
statement: For a finite Boolean word $x$, let $J(x)$ and $N(x)$ be the natural-number quantities assigned to it, and let $P(k)$ and $D(k)$ be the associated prefix and digit predicates. The language consists of exactly those $x$ for which $J(x)\ge 1$, $N(x)=P(J(x)-1)$, and $D(J(x)-1)$ holds.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define the quantities and predicates used in the membership condition, so their mathematical meanings cannot be stated more specifically.
